title: Spanish Animal Idioms: 25 Expressions Explained

body_html:
Spanish animal idioms are some of the most colorful expressions in the language, and some of the most useful. Spanish speakers describe a coward as un gallina (a hen), someone comfortable as como pez en el agua (like a fish in water) and a suspicious situation with aquí hay gato encerrado (there’s a cat locked in here). Many have no English equivalent, so knowing them helps you understand jokes, TV shows and family conversations. Here are twenty-five, grouped by animal.

Quick answer
  • Ser un gallina = to be a chicken, a coward.
  • Estar como pez en el agua = to be in your element.
  • Aquí hay gato encerrado = something fishy is going on.
  • Llevarse como perros y gatos = to fight like cats and dogs.
{{toc}}

Spanish animal idioms with cats and dogs

WordMeaningExample
aquí hay gato encerradosomething fishy is going onTanta amabilidad… aquí hay gato encerrado. (So much kindness… something’s fishy.)
dar gato por liebreto rip someone off (give a cat instead of a hare)En ese mercado te dan gato por liebre. (At that market they rip you off.)
buscarle tres pies al gatoto overcomplicate thingsNo le busques tres pies al gato. (Don’t overcomplicate it.)
cuatro gatoshardly anyoneEn la fiesta había cuatro gatos. (There was hardly anyone at the party.)
llevarse como perros y gatosto fight like cats and dogsMis hermanos se llevan como perros y gatos. (My siblings fight like cats and dogs.)
a otro perro con ese huesotell it to someone else, I don’t believe you¿Que estabas estudiando? A otro perro con ese hueso. (You were studying? Tell it to someone else.)
perro que ladra no muerdehis bark is worse than his biteTranquilo, perro que ladra no muerde. (Relax, his bark is worse than his bite.)

Birds, fish and farm animals

WordMeaningExample
ser un gallinato be a coward¡No seas gallina! (Don’t be a chicken!)
tener piel de gallinato have goosebumpsEsa canción me pone la piel de gallina. (That song gives me goosebumps.)
estar como pez en el aguato be in your elementEn la cocina está como pez en el agua. (In the kitchen she’s in her element.)
tener memoria de pezto have a terrible memoryTengo memoria de pez. (I have a memory like a sieve.)
ser la oveja negrato be the black sheepSoy la oveja negra de la familia. (I’m the black sheep of the family.)
matar dos pájaros de un tiroto kill two birds with one stoneMatamos dos pájaros de un tiro. (We killed two birds with one stone.)
estar como una cabrato be nuts (Spain)Tu tío está como una cabra. (Your uncle is nuts.)
ser un burroto be dumb or stubbornNo seas burro, pregúntale. (Don’t be stubborn, ask her.)
{{image:2}}

Wild animals and insects

WordMeaningExample
ser un linceto be very sharpPara los números es un lince. (She’s sharp with numbers.)
ser un zorroto be cunningCuidado, es un zorro. (Careful, he’s sly.)
lágrimas de cocodrilocrocodile tearsNo le creas, son lágrimas de cocodrilo. (Don’t believe her, those are crocodile tears.)
ser una tortugato be very slowEste internet es una tortuga. (This internet is so slow.)
cuando las ranas críen pelowhen pigs flyTe pagará cuando las ranas críen pelo. (He’ll pay you when pigs fly.)
¿Qué mosca te picó?what’s gotten into you?¿Qué mosca te picó hoy? (What’s gotten into you today?)
por si las moscasjust in case (casual)Lleva paraguas, por si las moscas. (Take an umbrella, just in case.)
ser un mosquita muertato look innocent but not beParece una mosquita muerta. (She looks like butter wouldn’t melt in her mouth.)

Por si las moscas (literally “in case of the flies”) is a fun, casual alternative to por si acaso, and it is very common in Mexico and Spain.

Why animal idioms are hard to translate

Animal idioms often reflect what animals mean in a culture. In English, a chicken is a coward and a fox is clever; Spanish agrees on both. But English has no common equivalent for gato encerrado or cuatro gatos, and English “a memory like a sieve” becomes a fish in Spanish. When I translate, I almost always replace the animal rather than keep it.

That is why word-for-word translation fails with idioms. I explain the general approach in {{link:english-idioms-in-spanish|English idioms in Spanish}} and {{link:literal-translation-mistakes-spanish|literal translation mistakes in Spanish}}.

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

A sample conversation

Laura: ¿Vas a ir a la fiesta de Marcos?
Are you going to Marcos’s party?

Toño: No sé. La última vez había cuatro gatos.
I don’t know. Last time there was hardly anyone.

Laura: Ándale, no seas gallina. Va a ir Sofía.
Come on, don’t be a chicken. Sofía is going.

Toño: ¿Sofía? Mmm… aquí hay gato encerrado. ¿Le dijiste algo?
Sofía? Hmm… something’s fishy. Did you tell her something?

Common mistakes

  • Ser un pollo for “to be a chicken”. The coward is un gallina. People often say un gallina for anyone, man or woman, though una gallina is also heard.
  • Llover gatos y perros. Animals don’t work here; it is llover a cántaros.
  • Using estar como una cabra in Mexico. It is understood but sounds Spanish; Mexicans say estar loco or estar zafado.

The RAE dictionary lists many of these expressions under the animal’s entry, which is a fun way to discover more. For proverbs with animals, such as camarón que se duerme…, see {{link:spanish-proverbs|Spanish proverbs}}.

{{image:3}} {{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Spanish animal idioms make your Spanish more vivid and help you catch jokes that would otherwise fly past. Pick five you like, listen for them, and use them when the moment fits. For more everyday expressions, see my guide to {{link:spanish-slang|Spanish slang}}.

faq.q: What are some common Spanish animal idioms?
faq.a: Ser un gallina, estar como pez en el agua, aquí hay gato encerrado, ser la oveja negra and llevarse como perros y gatos.

faq.q: How do you say “chicken” (coward) in Spanish?
faq.a: Ser un gallina or ser una gallina. ¡No seas gallina! means “Don’t be a chicken!”

faq.q: What does “dar gato por liebre” mean?
faq.a: To cheat someone by giving them something worse than promised, literally a cat instead of a hare.

faq.q: Are animal idioms the same in all Spanish-speaking countries?
faq.a: Most are shared, but a few are regional, such as estar como una cabra in Spain.
